questions: Did this walking problem begin suddenly, over minutes to hours?
Has it been getting progressively worse over days, weeks, or months?
Do you have new weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Do you have new trouble speaking, understanding speech, seeing, or swallowing?
Have you had severe back or neck pain?
Have you lost control of your bladder or bowels, or been unable to urinate?
Do you have numbness around your groin or inner thighs?
Do your legs feel stiff or difficult to move?
Do your feet feel as though they are stuck to the floor when you try to start walking?
Do you take small shuffling steps or have difficulty turning?
Do you have shaking or tremor when your hands or legs are at rest?
Have you noticed slowness or stiffness in your arms or hands?
Have you had increasing problems with memory, attention, or thinking?
Have you recently developed urinary urgency or frequent accidents?
Have you had repeated falls or near-falls?
Do you feel dizzy or as though the room is spinning when you stand or walk?
Do you feel unsteady mainly when your eyes are closed or in the dark?
Do you have double vision or abnormal involuntary eye movements?
Have you had a recent infection, fever, head injury, or loss of consciousness?
Have you ever had a stroke, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson disease, or another neurologic disorder?
Have you recently started or increased a medication that causes sleepiness, stiffness, or slowed movement?
Have you used alcohol or recreational drugs recently?
Is there any chance you could be pregnant?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder (functional gait disorder), without demonstrable structural, metabolic, peripheral nerve, or inflammatory neurologic disease

ALTERNATIVE 1: Idiopathic late-onset cerebellar ataxia

ALTERNATIVE 2: Hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia

ALTERNATIVE 3: Autoimmune or paraneoplastic cerebellar ataxia
